quizzes.title: Key terms across the lectures
quizzes.intro: Ten checks that the words of Lectures 1 to 4 mean the same thing to you as to an accountant.

questions.q: Which list contains only assets?
questions.explain: Assets are property the business owns. Capital and creditors are rights to that property, and sales is income.

questions.q: A supplier is owed money for yarn bought on credit. In the books of the buyer this is
questions.explain: The business owes the supplier, so the supplier is a creditor (a liability). A debtor is someone who owes the business.

questions.q: Which statement shows the position of a business on one particular date?
questions.explain: The balance sheet is a photograph on one date. The profit and loss account covers a period.

questions.q: Rent for twelve months is paid in advance on 1 January. On 31 January the unused eleven months are
questions.explain: Money already paid whose benefit belongs to later months is a deferral, shown as an asset (prepaid rent).

questions.q: Wages earned by workers in December but paid in January are, on 31 December,
questions.explain: The cost has built up but is not yet paid, so it is an accrual and a liability on the balance sheet date.

questions.q: The systematic charging of the cost of a machine to expense over its useful life is called
questions.explain: Depreciation spreads the cost of a fixed asset over the periods that use it.

questions.q: Drawings are an expense of the business and are deducted in the profit and loss account.
questions.explain: Drawings reduce the owner’s capital directly. They are not a cost of earning the income, so they do not appear in the profit and loss account.

questions.q: Under FIFO, the inventory left at the end of the period is valued at
questions.explain: First in, first out: the oldest goods are treated as sold, so what remains is priced at the latest purchases.

questions.q: Book value (written-down value) of a fixed asset is its cost less accumulated depreciation.
questions.explain: Each year’s depreciation is added to accumulated depreciation; cost minus that total is the book value.

questions.q: The trial balance is prepared mainly to
options: Check that total debits equal total credits
questions.explain: It lists every ledger balance; equal totals show that each entry was posted with both a debit and a credit.

quizzes.title: Linking the ideas
quizzes.intro: How the four lectures connect: one transaction, followed from the equation to the statements.

questions.q: Equipment is bought for cash. What happens to the accounting equation?
options: One asset rises and another falls by the same amount
questions.explain: Cash goes down and equipment goes up equally, so total assets, liabilities and capital are all unchanged.

questions.q: Why is an expense recorded as a debit?
options: Because it reduces the owner’s right to property, which is a credit balance
questions.explain: Capital is a credit balance. An expense decreases it, and a decrease in a credit item is a debit.

questions.q: Goods are sold for cash. The entry is
questions.explain: Cash (property) increases, so it is debited; sales increase the owner’s right, so Sales is credited.

questions.q: If closing inventory is overstated by Rs 10,000, then for that period
questions.explain: A higher closing inventory lowers cost of goods sold by the same amount, so profit and capital are both too high by Rs 10,000.

questions.q: When prices are rising, which method reports the lowest profit?
questions.explain: LIFO charges the newest, dearest purchases to cost of goods sold, so cost is highest and profit lowest.

questions.q: The net profit shown in the profit and loss account is added to the owner’s capital in the balance sheet.
questions.explain: Profit belongs to the owner: opening capital plus profit less drawings gives the closing capital.

questions.q: The monthly depreciation entry is
options: Debit Depreciation Expense, credit Accumulated Depreciation
questions.explain: The expense reduces capital (debit) and accumulated depreciation, which reduces the asset, is credited. No cash moves.

questions.q: A major repair that extends the life of a truck is
options: Added to the cost of the truck
Ignored until the truck is sold
questions.explain: A repair that extends life is capitalised, as with the Rs 13,300 added to Map Furniture’s truck. Routine repairs are expensed.

questions.q: Compared with straight line, declining-balance depreciation gives
options: Higher charges in early years and lower charges later
No depreciation in the first year
questions.explain: A fixed rate applied to a falling book value gives a large charge at first and smaller ones later.

questions.q: A trial balance that agrees proves that every transaction was recorded in the correct account.
questions.explain: Equal totals only prove the arithmetic of double entry. An amount posted to the wrong account still leaves the totals equal.

quizzes.title: Mixed calculations
quizzes.intro: Short calculations from each of the four lectures. State your answer in rupees unless told otherwise.

questions.q: A business has assets of Rs 850,000 and liabilities of Rs 320,000. What is the owner’s capital?
questions.explain: Capital = assets − liabilities = 850,000 − 320,000 = Rs 530,000.

questions.q: Sales are Rs 420,000 and total expenses Rs 365,000. What is the net profit?
questions.explain: Net profit = sales − expenses = Rs 55,000.

questions.q: Capital at the start of the year is Rs 600,000, profit for the year Rs 90,000 and drawings Rs 40,000. What is the closing capital?
Insurance of Rs 36,000 for twelve months is paid on 1 October. How much is still prepaid on 31 December?
questions.explain: Three months are used (Rs 9,000); nine months remain: 36,000 × 9 ÷ 12 = Rs 27,000.

questions.q: Opening inventory is Rs 25,000, purchases Rs 140,000 and closing inventory Rs 32,000. Find the cost of goods sold.
questions.explain: Goods available = 165,000; less closing 32,000 gives cost of goods sold Rs 133,000.

questions.q: Purchases were 100 units at Rs 50, then 100 units at Rs 60. 120 units were sold. Under FIFO, what is the cost of goods sold?
questions.explain: FIFO sells the oldest first: 100 × 50 + 20 × 60 = Rs 6,200.

questions.q: With the same purchases (100 units at Rs 50, then 100 at Rs 60) and 120 units sold, what is the value of the closing inventory under LIFO?
questions.explain: LIFO sells the newest first (100 at 60 and 20 at 50), leaving 80 units at Rs 50 = Rs 4,000.

questions.q: A loom costs Rs 3,000,000, has a residual value of Rs 300,000 and a useful life of 10 years. What is the annual straight-line depreciation?
A machine costing Rs 500,000 is depreciated at 20% on the declining balance. What is the book value at the end of year 2?
A truck with a book value of Rs 180,000 is sold for Rs 205,000. What is the gain on disposal?
questions.explain: Gain = cash received − book value = Rs 25,000.

quizzes.title: Case study
quizzes.intro: One small business, one month, ten questions. Keep your working: later answers build on earlier ones.

questions.q: What is the cash balance on 31 March?
How much does the business still owe its supplier (trade creditors) on 31 March?
questions.explain: Bought on credit 90,000, paid 50,000, so Rs 40,000 is still owed.

questions.q: What is the cost of materials used during March?
questions.explain: Purchases 90,000 less stock still on hand 30,000 = Rs 60,000 used.

questions.q: What is the depreciation on the machines for March?
questions.explain: 240,000 ÷ 5 years ÷ 12 months = Rs 4,000 a month.

questions.q: What are the total expenses for March (materials used, wages, rent and depreciation)?
What is the net profit for March?
What is Sana’s capital on 31 March?
questions.explain: Opening 500,000 + profit 31,000 − drawings 10,000 = Rs 521,000.

questions.q: What are the total assets on 31 March?
questions.explain: Cash 295,000 + materials 30,000 + machines at book value 236,000 = Rs 561,000, which equals creditors 40,000 + capital 521,000.

questions.q: How is the Rs 10,000 that Sana took home recorded?
questions.explain: Money taken by the owner for personal use is drawings. It reduces her right to the business (debit) and reduces cash (credit).

questions.q: If the closing stock of materials had been counted as Rs 35,000 instead of Rs 30,000, the profit for March would have been Rs 5,000 higher.
questions.explain: A higher closing stock means less material is charged as used, so expenses fall and profit rises by the same Rs 5,000.

quizzes.case: Sana opens a small stitching unit on 1 March. She puts Rs 500,000 into the business bank account; buys four sewing machines for Rs 240,000 cash (life 5 years, no residual value, straight line); buys fabric and thread on credit for Rs 90,000; pays the supplier Rs 50,000; makes cash sales of Rs 150,000; pays wages Rs 40,000 and rent Rs 15,000; and takes Rs 10,000 home. Materials still in stock on 31 March are worth Rs 30,000.

quizzes.title: Group challenge
quizzes.intro: Two-step questions that need more than one lecture at a time.

questions.q: A business starts the month with capital of Rs 200,000. During the month, sales are Rs 80,000, expenses Rs 65,000 and drawings Rs 5,000. Liabilities at month end are Rs 45,000. What are the total assets at month end?
questions.explain: Closing capital = 200,000 + 15,000 − 5,000 = 210,000; assets = liabilities + capital = 45,000 + 210,000 = Rs 255,000.

questions.q: Units available for sale: 200 at Rs 10, 300 at Rs 12 and 500 at Rs 15. 400 units remain at the year end. What is the weighted average cost per unit, in rupees to two decimals?
questions.explain: Total cost 13,100 ÷ 1,000 units = Rs 13.10 per unit.

questions.q: Using the same stock (200 at Rs 10, 300 at Rs 12, 500 at Rs 15; 400 units left), what is the cost of goods sold under FIFO?
questions.explain: 600 units were sold, oldest first: 200 × 10 + 300 × 12 + 100 × 15 = Rs 7,100.

questions.q: A machine is bought for Rs 800,000 with import duty of Rs 60,000, transport Rs 15,000 and installation Rs 25,000. Life 9 years, residual value Rs 90,000. What is the annual straight-line depreciation?
questions.explain: Cost = 900,000 (all costs to make it ready for use); (900,000 − 90,000) ÷ 9 = Rs 90,000.

questions.q: A machine costing Rs 100,000 with a 5-year life and residual value Rs 10,000 is depreciated by double declining balance. What is the depreciation in year 2?
questions.explain: Rate = 2 ÷ 5 = 40%. Year 1 leaves 60,000; year 2 charge = 60,000 × 40% = Rs 24,000.

questions.q: A truck cost Rs 400,000 and is depreciated straight line over 4 years with a residual value of Rs 40,000. It is sold after exactly 3 years for Rs 150,000. What is the gain on disposal?
questions.explain: Depreciation = 90,000 a year; book value after 3 years = 130,000; gain = 150,000 − 130,000 = Rs 20,000.

questions.q: A trial balance shows debits of Rs 21,550 and credits of Rs 21,350. Which error could explain it?
options: Rent of Rs 200 was debited but never credited to Cash
Rent of Rs 200 was debited to Wages instead
A sale of Rs 200 was not recorded at all
Equipment was bought for cash and both sides were recorded as Rs 200 too much
questions.explain: Only a one-sided entry makes the totals differ. The other errors keep debits and credits equal, so the trial balance would not reveal them.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of the initial cost of a new stenter?
questions.explain: Initial cost includes everything needed to get the asset in place and ready for use. Routine maintenance afterwards is an expense.

questions.q: Paying a creditor in cash reduces both total assets and total liabilities, and leaves capital unchanged.
questions.explain: Cash falls and the amount owed falls by the same figure, so the owner’s share is not affected.

questions.q: Rent of Rs 120,000 for one year was paid on 1 March. The accounting year ends on 30 June. How much rent expense belongs to this accounting year?
questions.explain: March to June is 4 months: 120,000 × 4 ÷ 12 = Rs 40,000. The other eight months are a prepaid asset.
